subject: BrightScale POC kickoff & working session - scheduling and success criteria
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara@brightscale.io>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightScale POC kickoff - scheduling & success criteria

Hi Maya,

Nice to e-meet you — thanks for taking this forward. BrightScale is ready to kick off the POC to validate routing + prompt routing behavior under our mixed-query workload. Our primary goals for the POC are:
- Validate prompt routing across two model variants (low-latency + cost-optimized)
- Run a 2-hour load window to observe latency distribution and KV cache hit rates
- Confirm quality baseline on our 25 scripted prompts (will share)

We are available next week on May 12th or 13th (PST) for the kickoff call and hands-on lab. Proposed windows:
- May 12: 10:00–11:30 PT
- May 13: 09:00–10:30 PT

Stakeholders who will attend: Michael Park (VP Eng), Lina Gomez (Head of Data), and our security contact (secops@brightscale.io).

Can you confirm which slot works and share a short agenda + any prep we should do (datasets, auth, test payloads)? We want the hands-on session to be the working hour — prompt review, routing matrix, and a short smoke load test.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Director of Product
BrightScale
[Attachment: BrightScale-PoC-constraints.docx (docx)]

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@brightscale.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightScale POC kickoff - scheduling & success criteria

Hi Sara — great to meet you and excited to run this with BrightScale.

May 13 at 09:00 PT works for our team; I penciled 09:00–10:30 PT for the kickoff + hands-on lab. Tentative agenda below (we'll share a PDF invite once confirmed):

1) 09:00–09:10 — Quick intros & success criteria (owners)
2) 09:10–09:35 — Prompt review and routing matrix walkthrough
3) 09:35–10:05 — Hands-on: routing demo + prompt tuning (we'll hand over a shell environment)
4) 10:05–10:20 — Short smoke load window (sample dataset)
5) 10:20–10:30 — Next steps & acceptance checklist

Prep notes / asks:
- Please share the 25 scripted prompts and one representative JSON payload set by EOD Tue (May 11).
- For the load window, can you confirm an expected RPS (approx)? That will help us size the temporary test harness.
- We'll need an engineer-level account for your team (API key) or a temporary shared test token; security will prefer the API key route.

We'll attach the kickoff agenda and a short runbook. Camila (cc'd) will lead the hands-on lab and routing review. I'll follow up with a calendar invite and a Drive link to the runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

— Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[m: +1 (415) 555-0192]
[Attachment: redwood-poc-agenda.pdf (pdf)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara@brightscale.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightScale POC kickoff - scheduling & success criteria

Thanks Maya — adding a few technical checklist items from our side.

Camila's tech notes (short):
- For routing matrix: please indicate which prompts we should route to the high-accuracy path vs low-latency path (we can help map by intent).
- Request sizes: what is the typical token length (avg and 95th)? If you can export a small sample (10–20 requests), that helps us pre-warm the KV cache strategy.
- Load window sizing: if you expect >50 RPS sustained we should run the load on dedicated capacity or use a burst policy to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Network: please whitelist these IP ranges (we'll include in Drive) if your environment restricts inbound callbacks.

I'll bring a routing matrix template to the call — attaching a CSV with the columns we'll walk through. Karthik, can you confirm you'll be available to monitor the load window and collect perf traces?

- Camila
Camila Reyes
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: routing-matrix.csv (csv)]

From: Sara Nguyen <sara@brightscale.io>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Park <michael.park@brightscale.io>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@brightscale.io>, poc@brightscale.io
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightScale POC kickoff - scheduling & success criteria

Perfect — May 13 at 09:00 PT is better for the execs. One small ask: can we split the session so the hands-on prompt review + routing happens during the kickoff (60–75m) and then run the longer 2-hour load test in a separate window on May 14? That lets our data team prepare a larger dataset and frees the execs from staying the whole time. Proposed plan:

- May 13, 09:00–10:15 PT — Kickoff + hands-on routing and prompt walkthrough (execs + eng)
- May 14, 13:00–15:00 PT — Dedicated load window (data eng only)

Stakeholders confirmed: Michael Park (VP Eng), Lina Gomez (Head of Data), Rahul Shah (Data Eng), and Tara Singh (Security).

RPS: Our initial estimate is 40 RPS average with 120 RPS spikes based on peak-hour traffic. Sample prompts & a 1000-record JSON for load will be uploaded to the Drive by EOD May 11.

Attaching BrightScale constraints doc. Please share the calendar invites and a short acceptance checklist we can sign off on.

Thanks,
Sara
[Attachment: BrightScale-PoC-constraints.docx (docx)]

Thanks — plan sounds good and we can split as requested. Calendar invites created:
- Kickoff + hands-on routing: Thu May 13, 09:00–10:15 PT (Google Calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=MWYxMm...)
- Load window: Fri May 14, 13:00–15:00 PT (separate invite sent to data eng list)

Quick acceptance checklist (we'll turn this into a Doc in Drive):

- API key or scoped test token provided (owner: BrightScale + secops)

Aditya — looping you in to confirm we can provision a short-duration dedicated pool if BrightScale's spikes look like 120 RPS during the test. Karthik will monitor traces and Camila will run the routing walkthrough.
